record.gate_rationale: The repeatable local probe establishes parser-derived field counts for every supplied old and new row in the declared Python 3.11.6 controlled fixture. It does not establish behavior for other parsers, malformed CSV, dialects, or museum inputs outside these samples.

gate_evidence.environment: Python 3.11.6 stdlib csv module; supplied controlled fictional museum samples in inputs/samples.json

record.rule: For field-count checks on these museum CSV inputs, count the fields returned by Python csv.reader. Do not infer the field count from the number of literal commas when a quoted field may contain a comma.
record.falsifier: Within the declared fixture environment, a supplied syntactically valid museum row has an expected three-field schema but Python csv.reader returns a field count other than three.
record.evidence_summary: The old header and two unquoted data rows each produce 3 fields by both literal splitting and csv.reader. In the new sample, A3 contains a quoted comma: literal splitting produces 4 pieces while csv.reader produces the expected 3 fields. The A4 escaped-quote row and the repeated header also produce 3 parser fields. This directly falsifies revision 1's comma-count rule while supporting parser-derived counts only in the declared fixture.
alternative_explanations: The old sample contains no comma inside a quoted field, so agreement there does not distinguish literal splitting from CSV parsing.
The observed mismatch is attributable to CSV quoting in the supplied data; the synthetic run metadata and seed role labels provide no independent live-team corroboration.
